Or ruining your life as you please. This is the most evident consequence of being free. That's why many people are incapable of being free (or better said, of accepting their freedom), because it means they are solely responsible for their mistakes. It’s very hard to admit that you’ve ruined your life, so it's much easier to give up freedom and let others decide for you. We place our destinies in the hands of our bosses, our family members, our politicians. That way, if something goes wrong, it’s always someone else’s fault. This is a very poor argument from my point of view.

I believe there is a clear interest in keeping things this way. Those in power want us to give up our freedom so they can keep pulling the strings. And if you don’t vote, do you think you’re rejecting the system? All the better for them. If you don’t engage in politics, they will do it for you, without a doubt, and they won't necessarily act in your interest.

I’ve always been fascinated by tarot cards. How can interpreting the order and cadence of cards in a deck reveal our future? Without delving into the science or pseudo-science behind it, I’d like tarot to work differently. What I’d like is for someone to read the cards for you, and you decide what you want to happen. That would be a good business.

I’m not sure how it would be paid for or what the business model would be, but I think the idea has potential.

I want to believe that’s how it is. Written in the cards, in the stars, everyone chooses their option, but we are the masters of our own future, responsible to the very end.

It amuses me how lately I hear serious concerns from the state about how badly things would go for Catalans if we became independent from the rest of the state. Scare stories about leaving Europe, abandoning the euro, economic ruin, and other bogeymen. And I say, well, what if it is so? A people can believe they are grown-up enough to make their own decisions and, if they are wrong, accept the consequences without fear.

Another amusing point is the firm belief that if the people were asked, the clear majority would say Catalans don’t want to be independent. Well, if that’s the case, so be it. But if it is, why not allow a vote? If in the end, it will turn out the way they prefer, right?

Or maybe not...

The point is, we don’t know yet. We don’t know because there’s no interest in making decisions, thinking, discussing, and acting. People moving forward means (they think) that they will stop moving forward.

The progress of others is a regression for me. What a perverse argument. Again, fear, the ghost that haunts all our operas.

I constantly see people around me who give in to fear and refuse to make their own decisions. Even though life, which is very wise, pushes them to do so again and again. But it’s still easier to trust the bank manager, the gym instructor, the euro-savvy scholar, in these times when a euro is a fortune.

At first, I felt some empathy when I encountered someone like that and tried to communicate and send out reality probes to see if they would land safely and finally, each one would take the helm of their life. I am less and less vehement and explicit now, and I’m starting to ignore their attitudes.

It never fails; they disappear from my life without remedy and without turning back.

We move on quicksand, and those who stand still sink. I move forward, fight for each step, each breath of air, and I realize the path is uphill. It’s hard, but you get higher and higher, and hard work has its reward. You can look back and see all that you have traveled and what you have now. Sadly, you also see what you leave behind (and who you leave behind).

The journey is worth it, this is very clear to me after years of struggle. I have tasted my freedom and do not want to give it up. I will take advice and follow those who have something to offer me as I always have, of course. I will continue to make mistakes, which has worked out well for me.
